standard_prerequisites.name: Local moving and centralizers
standard_prerequisites.statement: Centralizers are closed in any Hausdorff group topology. The author local homogeneity/patchwork inputs allow a supported homeomorphism in an open dendrite component moving one point while fixing another. The full support-centralizer identity and three-branch recovery801-831 are supplied.

core_obligations: Keep arbitrary Hausdorff group topologies in the comparison, not only Polish or separable topologies
Retain nonempty generalized-dendrite S and the branch-point topology identification
Keep support-centralizer characterization and three-branch reconstruction, not just the final union formula
Do not conflate universal minimality of a topology with a universal minimal dynamical flow
proof_roadmap: Express disjointness of a moved component from another component through closed centralizer conditions.
Deduce openness of all component-intersection sets in an arbitrary Hausdorff group topology.
Recover each branch-point stabilizer as unions of triples of those open intersection conditions.
Use branch-point stabilizers as the natural topology basis.
difficulty_reason: H2: the argument reconstructs the dendrite topology from purely group-theoretic centralizers and local supports, then uses median geometry of three distinct branches to recover open point stabilizers under an arbitrary Hausdorff group topology. This is a nonroutine topological-group reconstruction, with its full short core supplied; it does not follow merely from automatic continuity.
